spans.s: चमकसूक्तम् [camakasūktam], 1 The hymn containing च मे.
चमत्करणम् [camatkaraṇam] चमत्कारः [camatkārḥ] चमत्कृतिः [camatkṛtiḥ], चमत्कारः चमत्कृतिः f.
Poetical charm, that which constitutes the essence of poetry; चेतश्चमत्कृतिपदं कवितेव रम्या
] A kind of deer. -रः, -रम् A chowrie most usually made of the tail of Chamara.
The female Chamara; यस्यार्थयुक्तं गिरिराजशब्दं कुर्वन्ति बालव्यजने- श्चमर्यः
; केशेषु चमरीं हन्ति सीम्नि पुष्करको हतः Udb.; cf. चमरं चामरे स्त्री तु मञ्जरीमृग- भेदयोः Medinī. -Comp. -पुच्छम् the tail of Chamara used as a fan. (-च्छः) a squirrel.
चामरः [cāmarḥ] रम् [ram], रम् [चमर्याः विकारः तत्पुच्छनिर्मितत्वात्] also -रा -री sometimes.

A chowrie or bushy tail of the Chamara (Bos Grunniens) used as a fly-flap or fan, and reckoned as one of the insignia of royalty (and sometimes used as a sort of streamer on the heads of horses); व्याधूयन्ते निचुलतरुभिर्मञ्जरीचामराणि
; अदेय- मासीत् त्रयमेव भूपतेः शशिप्रभं छत्रमुभे च चामरे

; Ś.1.8. -Comp. -ग्राहः, -ग्राहिन्m. a person who carries a chowrie. -ग्राहिणी a waiting girl who carries in her hand a chowrie and waves it over the head of a king &c.; पृष्ठे लीलावलयरणितं चामर- ग्राहिणीनाम्
चामरिकः [cāmarikḥ], A person who carries a chowrie.
A vessel (can, ladle &c.) used at sacrifices for drinking the Soma juice;
A cake made of barley, rice &c. -Comp. -अध्वर्युः the priest who manages the drinking vessels. -उद्भेदः, -दनम् N. of place of pilgrimage where the river Sarasvatī is said to have burst forth.
चमसिः [camasiḥ], f. A kind of cake.
An army (in general); पश्यैतां पाण्डुपुत्राणामाचार्य महतीं चमूम्
A division of an army consisting of 729 elephants, as many cars, 2187 horse, and 3645 foot.
A grave. -Comp. -चरः a soldier, warrior. -नाथः, -पः, -पतिः the leader of an army, a general, commander;
चमूरुः [camūruḥ], A kind of deer; चकासतं चारुचमूरुचर्मणा Ś.1.8.
To drink, sip, drink off; चचाम मधु माध्वीकं
चम्पः [campḥ], [चम्प्-अच्] The Kovidāra tree. -म्पम् The flower of this tree.
A tree bearing yellow, fragrant flowers.
कम् A flower of this tree; अद्यापि तां कनकचम्पकदामगौरीम् Ch.
The fruit of a variety of plantain. -Comp. -चतुर्दशीf. The fourteenth day of the bright half of Jyeṣṭha.
माला N. of a neck-garment worn by women.
a kind of metre (see App.). -रम्भा a species of plantain.
चम्पकालुः [campakāluḥ], The jack or bread-fruit tree.
चम्पकावती [campakāvatī] चम्पा [campā] चम्पावती [campāvatī], चम्पा चम्पावती N. of an ancient city on the Ganges, capital of the Aṅgas and identified with the modern Bhagalapur.
The capital of the country of Aṅga i. e. Bhagalapur.
चम्पूः [campūḥ], f. A kind of elaborate and highly artificial composition in which the same subject is continued through alterations in prose and verse; गद्यपद्यमयं काव्यं चम्पूरित्यभिधीयते S.

; for instance भोजचम्पू, नलचम्पू, भारतचम्पू &c. -Comp. -भारतम् N. of a reproduction in prose and verse of the contents of the Mb. by Anantabhaṭṭa. -रामायणम् N. of a reproduction in prose and verse of the contents of the Rām. by Lakṣmanakavi.
चम्रिष् [camriṣ], a. Ved. Contained in the sacrificial vessel (as libations) (चमसस्थ) एष प्र पूर्वीरव तस्य चम्रिष;
The Dhattura plant. -Comp. -प्रख्य a. like gold.
चामुण्डा [cāmuṇḍā], A terrific form of Durgā;
; (the word is thus derived; यस्माच्चण्डं च मुण्डं च गृहीत्वा त्वमुपा- गता । चामुण्डेति ततो लोके ख्याता देवी भविष्यसि ॥).
चाम्पिला [cāmpilā], The river Champā; (perhaps the modern Chambal).
यम् Filament, especially of a lotus flower.
The Dhattura plant; m. (also in the last two senses).
